text:
maya: heads up — support escalated a p99 latency complaint from ACME. they say p99 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.8s around 2026-03-14 11:30 UTC. route: /v1/generate, model: redwood-7b-quant, tenant: acme-inc, avg qps ~0.1-0.2 (bursty). they attached a sample request and timestamps.

alex: reassigning to @jin for runtime investigation. could you check batcher metrics and any recent config rollouts? :eyes:

jin: on it. initial glance — we did a small canary yesterday that tweaked continuous-batcher max_wait_ms default from 50 -> 200ms and increased max_batch_size for conv models. Canary targeted dedicated hosts + a few low-qps tenants.

maya: they said this started after a deploy yesterday afternoon. i linked the customer timeline to our deploy window.

jin: that lines up. increasing max_wait_ms helps throughput for high qps flows, but for tiny QPS tenants it increases tail because requests wait for the timeout instead of being flushed quickly.

lisa: customer is on Dedicated with reserved pool but very low throughput. they rely on low-latency responses for interactive use.

alex: can we confirm whether this tenant hit a batching path that waited full timeout rather than flushing? metrics-bot, can you dump batcher.wait_time_p99 and batcher.queue_length p95 for the tenant over the last 6h?

metrics-bot: metrics query run. results (summary):
- batcher.wait_time_p99 (acme-inc): spiked from ~30ms -> 1.6s between 11:28-11:40 UTC
- batcher.queue_length p95: mostly 1-2, occasional bursts to 6
- route latency p99: 1.8s peak matching time window

jin: that confirms it — p99 aligns with batcher wait-time. small queue lengths but long wait (waiting for timeout). this is the continuous-batcher timeout effect.

alex: do we have quick mitigations? revert canary? or per-tenant override?

jin: short term options: 
1) rollback the canary (global) — quickest but hurts throughput for busy tenants.
2) set per-tenant batching policy: reduce max_wait_ms to 30ms for acme-inc (targeted fix).
3) set routing policy to send acme-inc to a low-latency variant that uses single-request flush.

maya: customer needs urgent fix. they asked for a workaround while we investigate. i recommended a temporary setting change if possible.

alex: do we have per-tenant override config in console?

jin: yes, we do. api: POST /internal/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/batcher-config with body: ```{ "max_wait_ms": 30, "max_batch_size": 8 }```

alex: can someone apply for acme-inc now and monitor? i'll coordinate with support and cs.

lisa: i'll message the account to say we're applying a short-term change and will follow up.

maya: applying now — callout: need approval from ops for Dedicated pool changes?

deploy-bot: policy check: per-tenant batching overrides allowed for Dedicated. ops approval not required for runtime config edits.

jin: thanks. after override, we should watch p99 and batcher.wait_time. metrics-bot, please add 1min refresh for these for next 30m and alert slack if p99 > 500ms.

metrics-bot: alert rule created: eng-sre/#batcher-watch — trigger if route p99 > 500ms for 2 consecutive 1m windows (for tenant acme-inc).

support-bot: note — customer informed of in-progress remediation.

maya: override applied: POST /internal/admin/tenants/acme-inc/batcher-config -> 200 OK. new config: max_wait_ms=30, max_batch_size=8.

metrics-bot: initial post-change samples: batcher.wait_time_p99 dropped to 38ms within ~30s. route p99 down to 120-180ms.

lisa: customer confirmed perceived latency is back to normal. they thanked us.

alex: great. still want root cause and long-term. jin — can you sketch why the canary increased risk for small-QPS tenants and what guardrails we should add?

jin: quick root-cause note: canary broadly increased max_wait_ms to 200ms to improve batching for high throughput workloads; however we lacked a per-tenant heuristic: small-QPS tenants shouldn't wait for max_wait_ms when queue length is low. two failure modes: (A) requests wait full timeout causing tail, (B) occasional bursts lead to larger-than-expected batching that increases end-to-end latency due to model runtime scheduling.

Suggested mitigations (longer-term):
- implement "adaptive wait" that scales max_wait_ms down when observed inter-arrival > threshold (i.e., low qps), or when per-tenant SLA low-latency flag is set.
- add automatic per-tenant default profiles (low-latency, throughput-opt). console flag to select.
- add canary gating: do not apply default batching param increases to tenants with avg qps < X during canary.
- extend rollout to include per-route AB tests measuring p95/p99 before committing defaults.

maya: can we also add a monitoring dashboard widget for "batcher wait by tenant"? it was harder to spot in the general heatmap.

jin: good idea. i'll add a tenant breakout to the batcher dashboard.

alex: assign followups: 
- jin: create a short RFC for adaptive wait and per-tenant profiles, include perf sims (due EOD + plan for canary change).
- obs-team/jun: add tenant-level batcher metrics to dashboard (due tomorrow).
- eng-sre: add alert for sudden p99 increases post-batching-rollouts (runbook).

jin: filing RFC draft now: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/XXX (will update).

deploy-bot: canary rollback not needed (targeted override applied). marking incident as "mitigated".

alex: thanks everyone. i'll close the loop with CS and the customer. please update thread when RFC / dashboard PRs land.

maya: closing — customer satisfied. leaving notes for postmortem and followups. :white_check_mark:
